Just over a year ago I was innocently riding my bike on the footpath just around the house we just moved too. We moved to a relatively small town with about 5k people from a town of about 40k, and since our neighbourhood was pretty quiet and the town was small we must of felt quite safe just hanging out near our property.

At about midday of a Monday (if I recall correctly) I was riding my bike at a decent speed and went to swerve around something, but my wheel got caught between the footpath and the nature strip and I fell off and smashed my arm. My mum initially just brushed it off with it being okay, but when she looked at it she realized it was fucked. So we had to ask our neighbour to drive us to the local hospital and that begins the 6 hour wait for an ambulance to get transferred to the larger hospital in the town we used to live in.

Little did we know that that day the ambulances were on strike. It probably would of been quicker to walk the 60km distance between the towns than sit at the hospital all day in agonizing pain.

The 6 hours come around. It's about 5:30 and the first ambulance comes around. They decide not to take me in that ambulance because I was in too much pain so a few minutes later another ambulance came and took me away. Nothing's more scarier than being taken away on a bed into an ambulance, considering the bed is quite narrow. You hope you don't fall off even though you're strapped in.

By the time we got to the larger hospital I had to move around the wrist I broke to do xrays. That has to be one of the most painful things I've ever done. The pain is describable until you break your wrist yourself. Any movements hurt like hell and the wrist feels ultra sensitive to anything.

Xrays are done now and it's probably about 8pm, and I'm about to go surgery. It's the first time (if I can remember) that I've ever had anesthesia (if that's the correct term, it's the one that makes you sleep) and I don't think I've ever been so nervous yet happy to do such a thing. On one hand (no pun intended) the pain will be over, and on the other I have to hope that the doctors don't put me to sleep permanently. The last point is absolutely ludicrous and I was definitely overreacting that day.

The surgery finishes and I wake up the next morning and I decide to have a shower. I go from being in pain to feeling like I'm lifting weights with an arm I just broke. The cast initially felt very heavy and that kind of surprised me. I have to put a plastic bag over the cast to have a shower. That's one of the weirdest things I think I've had to do at the expense of the environment. It was also very inconvenient to get dressed after showing as you have something on your arm that's like 3x the radius of what it normally is.

During the week I get transferred from the large town hospital to the one where I live. Until that Friday I just had to chill in hospital ( I got to go home a few times, I just had to come back to hospital at night) and watch TV. Luckily there was a night where some aviation shows were on. That left me pretty entertained for the night.

...

I'm out of hospital now. I'm at home and I still have the cast and I still have to shower with a plastic bag over it. It wasn't until a few weeks later that I had to get the cast removed.

...

The time to remove the cast comes around, I'm feeling genuinely nervous and I'm not sure what to expect. The doctor goes and cuts open the cast and releases my arm. The wrist that I initially broke was stiff, I couldn't move it at all. I had no problem moving my fingers though. I didn't want to look at my arm though, and I think I went a bit pale once the cast was cut open. Even now I sometimes can't mentally stand knowing that I have scars from stitches in my arm. It's one of the most disgusting things I think I've ever seen, and I watch a lot of liveleak and if you use it as well you'd know that there's a lot of content on there that the weak stomached can't handle.

I believe that's all the exciting things I have to say about my experience with biking.
